## Featured Project

### [Forecasting and Explaining U.S. Unemployment](capstone.qmd)

A reproducible machine-learning and historical-correlation study using six public U.S. macroeconomic series from **April 1956 through December 2025**. Six forecasting algorithms were evaluated at 3-, 6-, and 12-month horizons using chronological validation and simple baselines.

The selected **3-month Ridge Regression** model achieved **MAE 0.349, RMSE 1.020, and R² 0.720**. The selected **6-month Extra Trees** model retained moderate predictive value (**R² 0.563**), while the 12-month result had limited incremental value (**R² 0.205**). A separate lead–lag analysis identified **consumer sentiment** as the strongest overall external historical relationship with future unemployment, while also showing that relationships can change across economic regimes.
